source_request: Make a photorealistic image of an adult dockworker lifting the harbor water itself into a translucent curved flap beside the pier, with the flap still connected to the water below.
interpreted_intent: Literal physical handling of the water surface in an otherwise photographic harbor scene
subject: One adult dockworker physically handling the harbor's water surface
setting: A broad harbor pier at dawn with moored boats
event: The dockworker lifts one continuous region of the water surface into a curved translucent sheet that remains attached to the harbor
visual_priorities: Both hands visibly grip the same raised water region
The lifted water has a continuous, visible connection to the harbor
Curvature, refraction, and attachment ripples make the water's material response legible
The dockworker's crouch and reach look physically stable
baseline_prompt_en: A full-body documentary photograph of an adult dockworker crouching on a broad harbor pier at dawn. Both boots remain flat on the dry deck, knees apart, with the torso centered above the feet. Their two visible forearms extend forward with comfortably bent elbows; each hand grips the same lifted ridge of the harbor's water surface, thumbs above and curled fingers beneath. The water rises as one translucent, flexible sheet, still joined continuously to the harbor along its broad lower boundary. Its curved thickness refracts moored boats, while small ripples gather at the attachment. A clear side angle separates every finger, wrist, and sheet edge; the lifted water casts a faint caustic on the pier.
